title: Dimension bound for a scheme locally quasi-finite over a quasi-separated algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ a quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], $U$ an $S$-scheme, and $f:U\to X$ a representable locally quasi-finite morphism. Here quasi-separated means that the diagonal of $X$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Locally quasi-finite means that after every etale scheme chart $V\to X$, the morphism of schemes $U\times_XV\to V$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Here the fibre product is the sheaf fibre product of [def-trf-algebraic-space], represented by a scheme by the representability of $f$. With the atlas topology on $|X|$ [def-a1-space-point-topology] and topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], one has $\dim |U|\leq\dim |X|$. The convention is $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$.

source.place: Tags 0ABW (lemma-dimension-local-ring-quasi-finite) and 0A4J (lemma-dimension-decent-space), combined with Properties of Spaces Tag 0BAN (lemma-dimension); quasi-separated algebraic spaces are decent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-topological-dimension-local-rings] to the given quasi-separated $X$. In its notation put $D=\dim|X|=\sup_{x\in|X|}\delta_X(x)$. Here $\delta_X(x)$ is the chart local-ring dimension defined in the cited statement, not the dimension of open neighbourhoods of $x$. Consequently $\delta_X(x)\leq D$ for every $x\in|X|$, directly from the definition of supremum. This is the sole use of quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 03JX, lemma-bounded-fibres (quasi-separated implies decent), with definition-very-reasonable; Tag 0A4J, lemma-dimension-decent-space (2); spaces-properties.tex, Tag 0BAN, lemma-dimension (1)=(2), with Tag 04NA, definition-dimension-local-ring.

proof.text: Fix $u\in U$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-ring-dimension-quasifinite] to the given representable map $f:U\to X$. The product in both hypotheses is the sheaf fibre product, represented by a scheme since $f$ is representable. Its hypothesis is therefore precisely the chartwise locally quasi-finite hypothesis of the item, so it yields $\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}\leq\delta_X(f(u))$. Together with step 1 this gives $\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}\leq D$ for every $u$. No quasi-separatedness of $U$ or global finite-type hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0ABW, lemma-dimension-local-ring-quasi-finite. The chart definition and scheme agreement are spaces-properties.tex, Tag 04NA (definition-dimension-local-ring) and Tag 0BAM (lemma-pre-dimension-local-ring).

proof.text: By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], $\dim|U|=\sup_{u\in U}\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}$. For every $u$, step 2 followed by the supremum bound in step 1 gives $\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}\leq\delta_X(f(u))\leq\sup_{x\in|X|}\delta_X(x)=D$. Thus $D$ is an upper bound for the entire family indexed by $U$, and the least-upper-bound property gives $\dim|U|\leq D=\dim|X|$. This uses neither surjectivity of $f$ nor attainment of either supremum. For $U=\varnothing$ its supremum is $-\infty$, below every $D$. If $X=\varnothing$, a point of $U$ would map to a point of $X$, so $U$ is empty too and both dimensions are $-\infty$. The same inequalities apply when $D=\infty$.
